counterfactual_missing_items: Bacterial swab from malar lesions: Negative for growth
decisive_items: Numerous 1-2mm monomorphous pustules over background erythema on medial cheeks, chin, and nose
Exacerbation by sunlight exposure, especially in summer months
response.rationale: R4 has the most specific raw support: monomorphous pustules on sun-exposed areas and sunlight exacerbation, directly matching papulopustular rosacea. R1 is less specific, lacking the distribution and sunlight clue. R3 lacks the monomorphous pustule distribution and comedones; R2 is contradicted by negative bacterial swab; R6 lacks systemic symptoms and has mild pruritus.

rejected.why: Negative bacterial swab contradicts folliculitis, which is typically bacterial.
Acne vulgaris is less specific; lacks the monomorphous pustule distribution and comedones are absent.
Acne fulminans is severe and systemic, but patient has no systemic symptoms and only mild pruritus.
Redundant completion of R1 without additional raw support; R4 already provides the specific subtype.
